newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK jobs, earnings data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK jobs, earnings data.

text.p: Following is a selection of reactions to UK data showing December unemployment down 45,100 at 6.7 pct rate vs expected 30,000 fall and November average earnings up 4.0 percent y-y as expected.
GLENN DAVIES, CHIEF ECONOMIST, CREDIT LYONNAIS

"Another really quite large fall. We think the previous number was distorted a bit and there's now an unwinding of that distortion...But you can't deny the trend, unemployment is coming down...and the labour market must be tightening.

"The UK data are broadly in line with expectations and are unlikely to influence sentiment re this afternoon's monetary meeting. Key figure is underlying earnings which held steady at four percent. This suggests that a tightening labour market has not yet had any significant impact upon settlements. However it is hard to believe that, with unemployment falling as fast as it is, there will not be some knock-on effect before too long. and note that upcoming data will be boosted by a jump in bonus payments."

"Unemployment itself fell a measured 45,000. Even allowing for distortions caused by the jobseekers' allowance -- estimated at about 10,000 -- this constitutes a chunky decline and further emphasises the outperformance of the UK economy versus continental Europe. Accordingly ought to be taken well by sterling, notwithstanding the fact that most anticipate no rate hike this month. Data suggest that surprise drop in November manufacturing output was erratic and should be reversed, or revised away in due course."

"I think Clarke could go (on rates) tomorrow but on balance he might want to wait for anther three weeks.Then he would get the GDP figures for the fourth quarter and they've been a figure which seems to have influenced his decisions to move rates quite heavily in the recent past. That decision will clearly still be for a rate increase because the GDP figure for Q4, as indicated by the unemployment numbers, will be faster growing than it was in the third quarter."
MARIAN BELL, ROYAL BANK OF SCOTLAND

"A sharper than forecast 45,100 fall in December unemployment has been exaggerated by up to 12,000 by the jobseekers allowance, leaving the underlying fall only a little higher than the 30,000 consensus forecast. A slight gilt and short sterling negative but underlying average earnings growth remained at four percent and the Chancellor and the governor are unlikely to agree a rate rise today."
